svg.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: PCA9685: Typical application
svg.desc: Schematic of the PCA9685 typical application: the chip with U2 MCU, R1 resistor 4.7 kΩ, R2 resistor 4.7 kΩ, R3 resistor 10 kΩ, C1 capacitor 100 nF, R4 resistor 150 Ω, D1 led, J1 5 V supply; the MCU wires carry the port hooks GpioSet(CtrlPin::OutputEnable), Write() / WriteRead().
svg.text: Part of the data sheet's figure 26: the PCA9685 on an MCU's I2C bus with pull-ups on SDA and SCL, OE on an MCU output with a 10 kΩ pull-up, EXTCLK and A0 to A5 tied to VSS
(address 0x40, where figure 26 straps 0x55), and LED0 sinking one LED from 5 V through its resistor. With the LED from the supply the output is active low, so it takes
DirectLedPreset() (open drain, inverted). Figure 26 drives the other outputs through transistors, which this schematic leaves out; LED1 to LED15 are open here. Above each MCU
wire: the port hook that drives it. Datasheet: 10 Application design-in information, Figure 26, p. 35.

* Not confirmed in the datasheet: R1 4.7 kΩ: figure 26 leaves the value to UM10204 section 7; 4.7 kΩ suits 100 kHz and 400 kHz; R2 4.7 kΩ: figure 26 leaves the value to UM10204 section 7; 4.7 kΩ suits 100 kHz and

400 kHz; C1 100 nF: figure 26 shows no decoupling capacitor; section 10, question 2 advises one near the chip; R4 150 Ω: figure 26 gives no value; 150 Ω is about 20 mA for a 2 V LED from 5 V, under the 25 mA limit.
